When Design & Build is the right route

Design and Build works when the client wants a single point of delivery risk and is willing to accept the contractor's design responsibility. It underperforms when the design is intended to be highly bespoke and the client wants to retain aesthetic control past Stage 4 &mdash; in that case a traditional route with the architect retained is often better. Choosing the wrong contract is the most common expensive mistake on a mid-sized project.

The two levers that make D&amp;B work are the quality of the Employer's Requirements and the readiness of the design at novation. Weak ERs let the contractor's proposals drift from what was wanted; late novation with a partially designed scheme forces the contractor to price uncertainty into the lump sum. We work with clients and their PMs to get both settled before tender.

How we deliver, in order

  1. Brief & pre-construction studyUnderstanding of the client's outcome, budget, programme, planning position and any funding or lease constraints.
  2. Employer's RequirementsOutput specification, performance criteria, mandatory design solutions, room data sheets where warranted, and the contract preliminaries.
  3. Design team novationNovation of the architect and consultants to us at contract signature, or contractor-appointed design team where preferred.
  4. Tender or negotiationTwo-stage tender to selected subcontractors, or single-stage negotiation with our supply chain; Contractor's Proposals firmed against ERs.
  5. Design developmentStage 4 completion, statutory approvals (planning discharge, Building Control, party wall) coordinated with the contract programme.
  6. ConstructionEnabling works through superstructure, envelope, MEP and fit-out under one programme owned by one team.
  7. Commissioning & sign-offWitness testing, statutory sign-offs, warranty pack and Practical Completion.
  8. Aftercare & defectsRectification period, planned aftercare and the option to roll onto a maintenance contract with the same team.

Frequently asked questions

What is Design & Build?

A procurement route where a single contractor takes responsibility for both the design (developed in-house or by a novated design team) and the construction, under one contract, typically JCT DB 2016. The client's obligations are captured in the Employer's Requirements and the contractor's response is the Contractor's Proposals.

When is D&B better than traditional?

When the client wants a single point of design and construction responsibility, cost certainty against a coordinated design, and a shorter overall programme through overlap of design and construction. Traditional is often better when the client wants to retain the architect through construction to protect bespoke design intent.

What is novation?

Novation transfers the client's design appointments (usually the architect) to the contractor at contract signature. The design team completes the design under the contractor's direction from that point on, and the contractor takes on the design risk with them.

What is the difference between GMP and open book?

A Guaranteed Maximum Price fixes an upper limit for the works; savings below the GMP may be shared per the contract. Open-book delivery discloses actual subcontractor prices and preliminaries with an agreed contractor's fee, providing transparency at the cost of price certainty.

Who carries the design liability?

Under a D&B contract the contractor carries the design liability, backed by Professional Indemnity insurance held both by the contractor and by the novated design consultants (via collateral warranties or third-party rights).

What warranties does the funder or purchaser get?

Collateral warranties or third-party rights from the contractor and from the design team, plus manufacturer warranties on the envelope and roof, and a structural warranty (NHBC, LABC, BuildZone, ICW, CRL) on residential elements as required by the funder.
